newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak bourse listless, SAX firms on Slovnaft rise.
newsitem.headline: Slovak bourse listless, SAX firms on Slovnaft rise.

text.p: Trade on the Slovak Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday was hit by a lack of liquidity, though the SAX index increased by 0.51 points on gains to oil refiner Slovnaft.
Slovnaft closed up 15 crowns at 1,020, trading 261 shares on the BSE floor.
"Slovnaft's firming was no surprise, as there is a constant demand for the issue, but the volumes are still horribly low," Libor Briska of Creditanstalt said.
He added that Slovnaft and steel maker VSZ remained almost the only blue chips attracting investors.
VSZ closed unchanged at 745 crowns with 320 shares traded.
VSZ eased five crowns on Monday, after holding steady for several weeks.
"We have to wait whether this new price will be accepted by the market," Briska said. "I think the price is still pretty high, as the company announced a 40 crown dividend."
Briska said poor liquidity on the Slovak capital market was partially caused by turbulence on the neighbouring Czech money market, but added it might have also other reasons.
"Investors are now watching their positions on the money markets rather than trading with shares," he said.
"On the other hand, liquidity had dissapeared from BSE long before this happened to the Czech crown and it remains a long-term problem of the Slovak share market," he added.
Overall volume eased to 142,549 shares, from 180,080 shares traded on Monday, while turnover fell to 26.66 million crowns, from 276.96 million.
